mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% on a year-over-year basis signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% for three consecutive months) combined with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% monthly) signals improving purchasing power without cost-push inflation, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change falling from >0.3% to <0% within two months) signals labor market cooling, which reduces wage growth and input cost pressures, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate easing monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change drops from >0.3% to <0% within two months
regime_hint: transition from tight to loose labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
